topline.text: The story of the day: a new NASUWT survey finds 74% of teachers say poor pupil behaviour hurt their health and wellbeing last year, up from 62% in 2022.

DfE launched a £22.5m Enrichment Expansion programme yesterday for 400+ disadvantaged schools, funding clubs, sport and volunteering from January 2027 - Sheffield secondaries are among those included.
topline.action: Worth flagging to pastoral/enrichment leads now, ahead of January.

diary.text: National Alternative Provision Conference examines SEND reform and inclusion-first accountability.
DfE pupil premium quarter 2 payments for 2026/27 made to academies.
Midday deadline for Sheffield secondary school applications for September 2027 entry (national deadline 31 Oct).

sections.heading: National: poor behaviour 'corroding' teacher health, union warns

items.lede: NASUWT survey links severe pupil behaviour to worse teacher health.
items.body: Among teachers facing severe incidents, 70% reported headaches/migraines (v 61% of others) and a fifth said they'd been pushed or shoved by a pupil; only a third felt their employer dealt with incidents effectively.
items.action: Worth checking your incident-reporting and staff-support routes are actually being used.

sections.heading: National: enrichment funding reaches disadvantaged schools, Sheffield included

items.lede: £22.5m programme pairs 400+ schools with Enrichment Co-ordinators.
items.body: Delivered by the Youth Sport Trust, the scheme funds school clusters in deprived areas - including Sheffield sites - to map gaps in clubs, music, sport and volunteering, with support starting January 2027.

sections.heading: SEND: private special schools opt out of admissions duty

items.lede: Schools Week investigation finds independent special schools dropping off the Section 41 register.
items.body: Section 41 status normally obliges a school to admit any pupil named in their EHCP; some private providers are opting out to control their own capacity as the SEND places crisis and EHCP requests keep rising nationally.
items.action: Worth checking a setting's current Section 41 status before naming it in any MAPs pupil's EHCP.

sections.heading: South Yorkshire: house fire delays Rotherham primary's start

items.lede: Trinity Croft CofE Primary's school day was pushed back after a blaze shut the road.
items.body: South Yorkshire Fire and Rescue sent six engines to a house fire on Dalton Lane, Rotherham, on Monday morning; the school delayed its start to 10.30am while the road was closed and smoke cleared.

box.label: Jargon-buster - Section 41 register
box.intro: Came up in today's SEND story:
box.text: The DfE list of independent special schools approved to admit pupils on request. Being listed means a school must take a pupil if they're named in their EHCP, like a maintained school would; providers can choose to come off the list to control their own admissions.
